poster_title: Graph-Guided Concept Selection for Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Ziyu Liu, Yijing Liu, Jianfei Yuan, Minzhi Yan, Le Yue, Honghuai Xiong, Yi Yang

content: Graph-based RAG enhances retrieval in specialized domains with multi-hop reasoning.
Current methods incur high costs due to multiple LLM calls for entity and relation extraction.
G2ConS aims to reduce costs while maintaining QA performance.
High construction costs limit scalability of GraphRAG in enterprise settings.
Redesigning the pipeline can be costly and impractical.
Restricting graph structure affects retrieval accuracy on complex queries.
Core Chunk Selection reduces input chunks by removing low-ranked concepts.
Concept Graph Retrieval closes knowledge gaps at zero additional cost.
Dual-path retrieval leverages both KG and concept graph for efficient QA.
Ablation studies on MuSiQue dataset identify important concepts.
Evaluation on real-world datasets compares G2ConS with baselines.
Performance metrics include construction cost, retrieval effectiveness, and answering quality.
panels.figure_caption: Design and Results of Concept Deletion Experiment

content: G2ConS outperforms baselines in construction cost, retrieval effectiveness, and answering quality.
Average improvement of 31.44% across multiple metrics in MuSiQue.
Performance gains are consistent across different κ and λ values.
panels.figure_caption: Answer Quality by Varying κ and λ

content: G2ConS balances construction cost and QA performance for enterprise-scale systems.
Proposed methods can be integrated with existing GraphRAG approaches.
Future work will explore G2ConS in diverse domains and applications.
